status_contract.compatibility_field_scope: source preparation ONLY: the static artefacts for this family (pinned base and fix commits, hashed patches, oracle split, the licence decision for the exact pinned revision, and a window set by a verified ORIGINAL merge event) are complete. This is NOT a training release and NOT a data release: it carries no runtime, no independent licence countersignature and no permission-isolation evidence.
status_contract.contract: Two independent axes. Axis 1, source_preparation.status, is a static-artefact statement and is the ONLY thing the compatibility field `released` mirrors. Axis 2, training_release.status, is the release gate and additionally requires verified runtime oracle results on the actor environment, an independent licence review, demonstrated isolation of gold/dev/sealed material from the actor, and a constructed variant half. A consumer MUST read `training_release.status`; reading `released` and inferring a training approval from it is a contract violation. `released` is retained only so an existing consumer keyed on it keeps working, and it is scoped by the companion `released_scope` string that travels with it in every emitted file.
status_contract.why_two_axes: the previous revision published a single `released` boolean that mixed a static-artefact statement with a release decision, so a reader could mistake 'the hashes and the merge event are complete' for 'this task may train an agent'. Splitting the axes makes the release gate explicit and keeps the old key working for consumers that already read it.

withdrawn_windows.status: withdrawn 2026-10-05: never approved; superseded by the windows above. dev and sealed share ONE window and no ordering between them is claimed.

spec.time_axis_authority: a family's window is decided by the ORIGINAL upstream fix's MERGE event -- merged_at_utc of the pull request the fix commit belongs to, recorded with its metadata source and raw-response hash. The commit's own author and committer dates are kept ONLY as audit corroboration: a rebase, squash or re-land can rewrite them, so they never qualify a family. Release/tag dates, snapshot or pin dates, backport dates and cherry-pick dates are rejected substitutes.

merge_evidence_artifact.policy: the ORIGINAL family fix's upstream MERGE event: the merged_at_utc of the pull request whose merge_commit_sha equals the fix commit
merge_evidence_artifact.missing_merge_evidence: status=unverified, window_qualified_by_merge_event=false, counted in no window. An issue reference in the commit message is not merge evidence and can never promote such a record.

spec.snapshot_axis_is_separate: the pinned revision decides which CONTENT exists (the fix commit must be an ancestor of it); it never decides which WINDOW a family belongs to.
spec.p0_requirement: 8 training families = 4 real + 4 variant, from >= 2 repos
spec.issue_text_policy: No upstream issue/PR prose is copied into the deliverable. Only the numeric issue reference is recorded for traceability; every task statement is rewritten from the observed defect, per the integrated review's rule that code being open source does not license its comments.
spec.runtime_verification_status: not_run_in_d0: the D0 research runtime has no reachable package index, so pytest could not be installed and no FAIL_TO_PASS run was executed. Every field below is derived statically from the pinned git objects. Building the environment and actually running the oracle is E0's deliverable, and the 8-task cross-check is later engineering acceptance.
spec.variant_release_policy: variant families are released=false by construction: their variant commit does not exist until an author builds it. Only the upstream source base commit is pinned, so no record can be published with an empty SHA.

families.upstream_subject: Fix is_bool_flag being set to True even if is_flag is False
families.symptom_restatement: An option object reports itself as a boolean flag whenever its value type happens to be boolean, even when it was never declared as a flag. Downstream code that branches on that report therefore takes the flag code path for ordinary options, so a plain option with a boolean value type is treated as something the user can toggle. The task is to make the reported flag-ness depend on the declaration and on the value type together, so a non-flag option reports False while a genuine flag still reports True.
families.failure_mechanism: flag-ness predicate tests only the value type and ignores the declaration

families.mutation_recipe: On top of the real family's base_commit, move the flag-ness predicate out of the option constructor into a module-level helper that the constructor calls, and have a second consumer read flag-ness through that helper on a different code path (the help/usage rendering path) instead of the stored attribute. Leave the helper's body with the same defect the real family fixes. Re-express the task text against the helper's new name and location.

summary.honest_position: the oracle material is withheld from the public artifacts, but ISOLATION IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the upstream repositories are public and this delivery demonstrates no actor-side network or history control. Any consumer must treat these families as gold-withheld-but-publicly-discoverable until the custodian produces negative permission tests.

actor_isolation.scope: the training/search actor, not the D0 author

gaps.statement: every counted family comes from a public upstream repository whose history contains the original fix. An actor with network access can find it. No sandbox, proxy rule or deny-list is demonstrated here, and D0 is not the party that can demonstrate it.
gaps.what_would_close_it: a negative test showing the actor environment cannot reach the upstream remote, plus a run recorded without network

gaps.statement: the pinned clones here carry FULL history (they had to, to mine the families). If the actor receives such a checkout, the fix commit is reachable by `git log`. The actor's checkout has no demonstrated history truncation and no demonstrated future-history control.
gaps.what_would_close_it: hand the actor a base-commit-only checkout (no descendants, no future commits) and record a negative test that the fix is not reachable from it, including via reflog, packed refs or remotes

gaps.statement: restricted-oracle.json still carries split_declaration_pending: a custodian holding the gold material has not ruled which split its contents belong to. Naming a file 'restricted' establishes nothing.
gaps.what_would_close_it: the custodian adjudicates the split and records who may read it

actor_isolation.note: none of these gaps blocks the static source-preparation work; all three block the training-release gate, which is why training_release.status is 'blocked' for every family
